items.title: GlobalComix's AI-Powered Refresh Looks a Lot Like Its Competition
items.excerpt: Digital comics platform GlobalComix relaunched with an AI chatbot that recommends titles and answers reader questions, plus AI-generated page descriptions and new creator profiles; the Beat asks whether the redesign just mirrors rivals.

items.title: Getbackers Manga Gets Comic Anime From AI Platform MangaNow Studio
items.excerpt: AI platform MangaNow Studio is turning the 1999 manga Getbackers into a 'comic anime' that animates the original manga pages; it debuts on YouTube on December 1.

items.title: Digital Fatigue, Book Bans, and AI: SCBWI's 2026 State of the Industry Overview
items.excerpt: SCBWI's children's book marketplace webinar on November 13 weighed AI alongside book bans and digital fatigue, covering how AI is reshaping picture-book illustration, submissions and creator contracts.

items.title: Literary Translators Warn AI Threatens Their Livelihoods in Copyright Case
items.excerpt: The American Literary Translators Association's amicus brief in the authors' suit against OpenAI and Microsoft argues AI translation could turn translators 'from interpreters into primarily editors of large language model output'.

items.title: New analysis finds no evidence of racial bias in Pangram
items.excerpt: A new analysis finds no evidence that cultural differences in writing style make the AI detector Pangram return false positives, though it doesn't rule out bias in how accusations are made; follow-up to the Esquire debate.

items.title: Just-in-Time Synthesis: A New Approach to an Old Genre
items.excerpt: Compares a commissioned review article with an AI-generated just-in-time overview answering the same reader need, asking how each is made and whether a reader can tell the difference.

items.title: The Anatomy of 'Harm': An Interview with IFRRO CEO Anita Huss-Ekerhult on AI and Copyright
items.excerpt: IFRRO's CEO discusses the federation's study detailing the harm generative AI causes publishers and authors, and what collective licensing can do about it.

items.title: AI Is Changing the Book Business. The Literary Community Is Pushing Back
items.excerpt: Sacramento-area booksellers refuse to stock AI titles and Sibylline Press rejects manuscripts suspected of AI text, while indie authors blame floods of AI books for falling KDP sales despite Amazon's new two-titles-a-week cap.

items.title: Can AI bring literature to more readers? Authors weigh opportunities and challenges
items.excerpt: At the Sharjah International Book Fair, authors debated whether AI can expand literature's reach through translation and accessibility while preserving emotional depth and cultural identity.

items.title: Pay us for our IP or we'll sue, News Corp boss tells AI labs
items.excerpt: News Corp chief Robert Thomson, whose group owns HarperCollins, warned AI developers that refuse to discuss redress for content used in training that the company will sue.

items.title: 뤼튼, 크랙 오리지널 콘텐츠 IP로 키운다…웹툰·게임 확장 청사진
items.excerpt: 뤼튼테크놀로지스가 지스타 2026에서 AI 캐릭터·스토리 플랫폼 '크랙'에서 만들어진 자체 콘텐츠를 웹툰·웹소설·게임 IP로 확장하겠다는 청사진을 발표했다.

items.title: [서울국제예술포럼] "AI가 소설판 장악하는 미래?… 그래도 사람은 쓸 것!"
items.excerpt: 17일 DDP 서울국제예술포럼에서 소설가와 연구자들이 생성형 AI가 '완벽한' 글을 쓰는 시대에도 사람이 계속 쓸 이유와 문학 창작의 변화를 논의했다.

items.title: BP Interview Exclusive: Simbarashe Steyn Kundizeza on Weathering the AI Controversy and Reclaiming His Caine Prize Moment
items.excerpt: After a month-long forensic review cleared his Caine Prize-winning story of AI use, Zimbabwean writer Simbarashe Steyn Kundizeza talks about the accusations and reclaiming his win.

items.title: AI is giving writers the support publishing cannot
items.excerpt: Comment by writer Marian Stan, whose work explores AI, creativity and authorship, arguing that AI tools are filling editorial and developmental support gaps that traditional publishing no longer provides to writers. (Body partly paywalled.)

items.title: Australian Society of Authors, Australian Publishers Association among orgs launching 'Not AI's to Take' campaign
items.excerpt: The ASA, APA and other creative and media bodies launched a national campaign and petition demanding AI companies get permission and pay before training on Australian creative work.

items.title: AI sparks debate among writers at Concord conference
items.excerpt: At a large New Hampshire writers conference, SF author James Patrick Kelly and others debated how AI and 'AI cops' are complicating the act of writing fiction.

items.title: 'In the Age of AI, Whose Is Poetry?'... Song Hyegeun, Born in 2001, Wins Kim Soo-young Literary Award
items.excerpt: Poet Song Hyegeun won the 45th Kim Soo-young Literary Award for poems exploring the poetic possibilities of the AI era through memes, game and digital language.

items.title: 구글플레이 올해의 앱·게임...네이버웹툰 '컷츠메이크'·넥슨 '메이플 키우기'
items.excerpt: Google Play named Naver Webtoon's AI creation tool CutsMake, which turns webtoon scenes and characters into short-form videos, its Best App of 2026.

items.title: Publishing Ireland conference: AI and rising costs high on the agenda
items.excerpt: Report from the Publishing Ireland annual conference where AI's impact on publishing and rising production costs dominated discussion among Irish publishers. (Body partly paywalled; AI confirmed in headline only.)

items.title: The latest AI threat to books
items.excerpt: New Zealand ghostwriters of celebrity and sports memoirs report falling commissions and requests to edit AI-generated manuscripts, arguing AI lacks the interviewing and empathy memoir requires.
